title: Return after a body halts
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and let $m$ be either Boolean mode. Let $c$ be a configuration of $B$ on input $x$, let $t$ be a positive integer, and choose a word $w$ and a fuel-machine configuration. Suppose the run of $B$ from $c$ does not halt at any time $u<t$, does not visit state $a$ at any strictly intermediate positive time, and is halted at time $t$. Then the loop host, started in the call configuration corresponding to $c$ with release flag set and no flag bit, reaches after $t$ steps the call configuration corresponding to the run of $B$ at time $t$, with release flag unset and the flag bit set; the word, fuel configuration, input, and other call data are retained.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean finite Turing machines B and F
body run is unhalted at every time u<t
body run avoids the anchor at strictly intermediate positive times
body run is halted at time t
